newsitem.title: CHINA: China's refineries to import more oil in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China's refineries to import more oil in 1997.

text.p: China will import more oil in 1997 for processing by refineries and boost production of natural gas to meet growing domestic demand, the China Daily said on Saturday.

"Surging demand for finished oil and relatively stable supply of onshore oil have forced refineries to look into overseas markets," the newspaper quoted China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) president Sheng Huaren as saying.
Sheng did not say how much oil imports would increase.
China imported 18.4 million tonnes of oil in the first 10 months of 1996, up 63 percent from the same 1995 period.
Sinopec's refineries processed 20 million tonnes of imported oil in 1996, accounting for 20 percent of the total amount processed, the newspaper said.
The refineries would process more imported oil in 1997, he said.
China produced an average of 3.0 million barrels of oil (bpd) a day in 1995, the newspaper said. The figure was expected to climb to 3.3 million bpd by the year 2000.
Domestic demand for finished oil averaged 3.04 million bpd and was expected to hit 3.9 million bpd by 2000, it said.

Separately, China plans to double its annual natural gas production capacity to 30 billion cubic metres (1.06 trillion cubic feet) by 2005, the newspaper quoted an official of the China National Petroleum Corp as saying.

China was expected to verify additional onshore gas reserves of 1.0 trillion cubic metres (35.35 trillion cubic feet) by 2000, with the total hitting 2.0 trillion cubic metres (70.7 trillion cubic feet), it said.
